headline: Host context and diet shape mobile elements and genome content in gut bacteria
label: Gut Microbiome Mobile Element Ecology
summary: Recent preprints and publications map plasmid, phage and metabolic determinants of gut bacterial genome content across large cohorts.
synthesis: The dominant thread is how mobile genetic elements and host or environmental context structure gut bacterial genomes. The ETEC preprint reports contrasting plasmid-host associations that shape the distribution of enterotoxigenic E. coli colonization factors. The TwinsUK study assembles a 116,740-vOTU phage catalogue from 1,069 gut metagenomes and links phage genomic variation to bacterial species and microbial metabolites. Genome-scale models of 105 C. difficile strains show that diet shifts commensal interactions more than strain differences do, although this work addresses metabolic interplay rather than mobile elements directly. Other studies extend the scope: MiSA detects disease-associated spatial dysbiosis in HiPR-FISH images, and metaEukaryome uses mitochondrial and plastid sequences to detect eukaryotes across 75,727 global metagenomes. Together these point to host and environmental context as key determinants of gut genome content, though only the ETEC and phage studies examine mobile elements explicitly.
